collisions: Unit is the claim. A codex card can hold two claims; each gets its own home. Five cards sit in two Concordance rows and are split by claim (section 11).

Adaptive-other rule. A claim belongs here only if its truth depends on an opponent, rival or counterpart who reacts. A choice against a non-reacting environment is EC.O.A1 (decision) or MA.B.C4 (operations research). CONTESTED exception: ST.O.A5.3 and ST.O.A5.4 are kept, because the corpus treats markets and nature as environments whose response to exposure is adversarial in effect. Alternative: move both to EC.O.A1.
Threat rule. If the operative move is a conditional threat to impose cost, the claim is ST.O.A3, whatever the instrument. A move that restructures the game without a threat is ST.O.A2.

Medium rule. Land, sea, air, space, cyber and the information environment are substrates. Coercion through a medium is A3; force applied in it is A4; information created, stolen or corrupted in it is A5.5.
Level rule. Tactical, operational, strategic and grand-strategic are a scale, not cells [luttwak-c17]. A claim about the levels themselves is ST.O.A4.1.
Case rule. A dated event (Cannae, Barbarossa, Cuba 1962) is a case. It is evidence handled by ST.M.B4; its historical truth uses HI.O.A1.
Game rule (from MA and EC). The theorem is MA, the allocation is EC, the choice of game is ST. Test: does the claim change if the opponent can change the game? If yes, ST.
Politics rule. Why polities go to war is PO.O.A5.1 (Fearon's bargaining failure). How a party coerces or fights is ST.
Business rule. The firm's conversion, cost, capital and governance are BU.O.A3. Positioning against rivals who react is ST.
Mind rule. A cognitive bias as a process is MS. Its exploitation or correction against a counterpart is ST.O.A5.2.
Law and philosophy rule. Whether a use of force is lawful is LA. Whether it is just is PL. Whether it works is ST.
Artefact rule. How a weapon or exploit works is EN or CS. What it does to the contest is ST.
Existence and solution theorems of games (minimax, Nash, Shapley, Rubinstein, folk theorem, Blotto, Lanchester) → MA.B.C4 (91A)
Equilibrium as market allocation; Cournot, Bertrand; adverse selection as market failure → EC.O.A2
Decision against a non-reacting environment; loss-aversion coefficient → EC.O.A1
Contract and principal–agent theorems → EC.O.A3.1
The firm's operations, cost, capital and governance → BU.O.A3
Theory of the international system; anarchy; war onset as bargaining failure → PO.O.A5.1
Civil-war onset (greed versus grievance) [future_of_war-c16]; climate and conflict [future_of_war-c23] → PO.O.A3 (climate system: EA)
Cognitive biases as processes → MS
open: whether deterrence success can be warranted at all beyond W6 on non-events.

the corpus's silences — logistics, operational art, alliance theory, economic statecraft, civil–military relations, strategic culture, arms control, space power, AI and autonomy. Each has a home (section 4) but no card.
codex card content not yet verified against the source books (R11).
the Encyclopedia's Panel reaches 14 of 27 Concordance rows by name; 13 rows are reachable only by tag (prototype section 13).
